module Gopurs.ModuleWorkers (declaration) where

import Prelude
import Data.Array as Array
import Data.Map as Map
import Data.Maybe (Maybe(..))
import Data.Tuple (Tuple(..), fst, snd)
import Effect.Ref as Ref
import Effect.Unsafe (unsafePerformEffect)
import Gopurs.ExprAnalysis (extractExprFuncType, functionResultAfter, getExprType)
import Gopurs.ExprContext (ExprContext, TranslateExpr, bindParameters, flattenStmts)
import Gopurs.GoAst (GoDecl(..), GoExpr(..), GoType(..))
import Gopurs.GoSymbol (GoReference(..), generated)
import Gopurs.GoConversions (boxGoExpr, coerceGoExpr)
import Gopurs.GoFunctions (Parameters, curriedFunction, iterationBindings, loopParameters, namedParameters)
import Gopurs.Int32Loops as Int32Loops
import Gopurs.AffineLoops as AffineLoops
import Gopurs.ArraySnoc as ArraySnoc
import Gopurs.ListFilter as ListFilter
import Gopurs.TailAddLoops as TailAddLoops
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.Codegen.Tco (TcoExpr)

type Worker =
  { ident :: String
  , args :: Array String
  , body :: TcoExpr
  , val :: TcoExpr
  }

-- Use precisely the ABI published by ModuleBindings, including native record
-- projections. A self-recursive singleton gets a loop; peers in larger groups
-- remain ordinary calls. Module bodies begin with no captured local bindings.
declaration :: TranslateExpr -> ExprContext -> Boolean -> Worker -> GoDecl
declaration translate context@{ codegenStateRef, modNameStr, moduleFunctions } isSelfRecursive fn =
  let
    info = Map.lookup fn.ident moduleFunctions
    params = namedParameters fn.args (case info of
      Just signature -> signature.fArgs
      Nothing -> [])
    expectedBodyType = map (functionResultAfter (Array.length fn.args)) (extractExprFuncType (getExprType fn.val))
    loop = if isSelfRecursive then
      [ { ident: fn.ident, loopParams: map fst (loopParameters params), goTypes: map snd params } ]
      else []
    workerContext = context
      { depth = 0
      , bound = bindParameters params Map.empty
      , tcoIdent = Just fn.ident
      , loopCtx = loop
      , options = { isTail: isSelfRecursive, inEffectBlock: false }
      , mbExpectedExprType = expectedBodyType
      , mbExpectedGoType = if Array.null fn.args || resultType == TypeValue then Nothing else Just resultType
      }
    resultType = case info of
      Just signature | Array.length fn.args < Array.length signature.fArgs -> TypeValue
      Just signature -> signature.fRet
      Nothing -> TypeValue
    tailAdd = if isSelfRecursive then
      TailAddLoops.worker translate workerContext fn.ident params resultType fn.body
      else Nothing
    body boxed = case tailAdd of
      Just loopBody -> loopBody
      Nothing ->
        let
          native = case ListFilter.worker context.metadata params resultType fn.val of
            Just filtered -> Just filtered
            Nothing -> ArraySnoc.worker modNameStr fn.ident params resultType fn.body
          result = case native of
            Just lowered -> lowered
            Nothing -> translate workerContext 0 fn.body
          returning = if boxed then boxGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr result.expr result.exprType
            else coerceGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr result.expr result.exprType resultType
          statements = flattenStmts result.stmts <> [ GoReturn returning ]
        in if isSelfRecursive then
          AffineLoops.wrap (AffineLoops.globalTarget modNameStr fn.ident) params resultType fn.body
            (Int32Loops.loop fn.ident params resultType statements)
          else GoBlock (iterationBindings params <> statements)
    value = if Array.null fn.args then
      -- A zero-argument abstraction still defers its whole body until called.
      curriedFunction [ Tuple "_" TypeValue ] TypeValue
        (body true)
      else
        let
          worker = GoFunctionDecl
            { name: generated modNameStr ("Call_" <> modNameStr <> "_" <> fn.ident)
            , params: loopParameters params
            , result: resultType
            , body: body false
            }
        in
          unsafePerformEffect do
            Ref.modify_ (\state -> state { declarations = Array.snoc state.declarations worker }) codegenStateRef
            pure (boxedWrapper context fn.ident params resultType)
  in
    GoCachedValue { identifier: generated modNameStr (modNameStr <> "_" <> fn.ident), expression: value, goType: TypeValue }

-- Module wrappers group up to ten arguments; larger arities keep unary layers.
-- LocalWorkers and anonymous closures retain their own grouping policies.
boxedWrapper :: ExprContext -> String -> Parameters -> GoType -> GoExpr
boxedWrapper { codegenStateRef, modNameStr } name params resultType =
  let
    wrapperParams = map (\(Tuple param _) -> param <> "_box") params
    call = GoCall (GoRef (SymbolReference (generated modNameStr ("Call_" <> modNameStr <> "_" <> name))))
      (map (\(Tuple param ty) -> coerceGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr (GoVar (param <> "_box")) TypeValue ty) params)
    boxed = boxGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr call resultType
    arity = Array.length params
    wrapperName = if arity == 1 then "gopurs_runtime.Func" else "gopurs_runtime.Func" <> show arity
  in
    if arity <= 10 then
      GoCall (GoVar wrapperName) [ GoFuncLit (map (\param -> Tuple param TypeValue) wrapperParams) [] boxed TypeValue ]
    else Array.foldr
      (\param inner -> GoCall (GoSelector (GoVar "gopurs_runtime") "Func")
        [ GoFuncLit [ Tuple param TypeValue ] [] inner TypeValue ])
      boxed wrapperParams

CHANGELOG.md.text:
# Changelog

All notable changes to gopurs are recorded here. The format follows
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) and the project uses
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).

## [Unreleased]

### Changed

- Reduce affine countdowns containing unused global binding reads. Retain the
  first iteration's strict reads in order on the guarded positive path, and
  preserve the original loop for zero, negative or wide inputs.
- Emit native integer multiplication when operand bounds prove an exact
  product within the JavaScript Number integer range. Expose those bounds for
  counted translations while retaining ordinary IntMul semantics elsewhere.
- Reduce proven closed integer countdowns after thunk fusion, allowing existing
  affine loop optimization to eliminate repeated calls. Preserve strict reads,
  exact Int32 addition semantics and runtime input boundaries.
- Reduce fully consumed compositions of counted integer translations to guarded
  arithmetic. Preserve opaque runtime inputs, exact repeated-addition Int32
  semantics, and the original computation outside the proved input domain.
- Evaluate bounded closed recursive integer computations and record projections,
  retaining strict global reads and unknown computations. Bound interpreter
  work and stack depth separately, and allocate fresh residual bindings.
- Construct annotated Tuple results directly in the native representation
  required by their consumer, avoiding boxing and reconversion of composite
  fields while preserving the TAST and the existing public representation.
  Preserve constructor payloads and sum tags when converting native values
  to worker return values.
- Preserve boxed composite producers across annotations and local bindings
  until a consumer requires a native representation. Keep instantiated array
  and ADT-pointer payloads in native Tuple worker results; public wrappers
  retain the canonical boxed representation.
- Share literal record keys across allocations for records with one to five
  fields. Store two-Int records compactly while preserving immutable updates,
  field lookup and foreign conversion behavior.

## [0.1.1]

First final release, prepared from the RC20 compiler and pinned libraries.
Correct the recovery command's cyclic module import without rebuilding or
changing the qualified compiler.
Qualification and publication are recorded in the live
[quality record](https://github.com/0x000000000000000000001/gopurs/blob/main/docs/quality-0.1.0.md).

- Compile the typed PureScript fork's TAST to Go with JavaScript or native
  compiler hosts, Release/Dev profiles and incremental compilation.
- Write ordinary Go FFI for values, records, callbacks, effects and cancellable
  asynchronous operations. The typed frontend is pinned to
  `ae6a6f644502bafcfa4fa94d8f81a1a1a1ca5080`; stock `purs` is not a substitute.
- Include RC20's callback, return-arity and ignored-Unit corrections, and the
  Foreign port's native readers preserving shared/cyclic child values.
- Refresh generated-code references against the preserved TAST types. Keep
  original compiler qualification and benchmark identities when reusing their
  exact bytes; record final packaging and fixture producers separately.

The supported reference is Node.js 24.8.0 and Go 1.27.0 on Linux amd64,
Linux arm64 and macOS arm64. This is a `0.x` release; the
[compatibility policy](docs/publication-scope.md) and
[limitations](docs/limitations.md) define its scope. The
[RC20 benchmark](https://github.com/0x000000000000000000001/gopurs/blob/main/docs/release-benchmark.md#completed-rc20-campaign--13-november-2026-utc)
measures backend generation, not application runtime.

## [0.1.0] — not published

Signed tag `v0.1.0` remains available for traceability. Its CI stopped before
fixture execution or packaging because the artifact-acquisition command had
a cyclic module import. No npm package or GitHub release was published.
Version `0.1.1` resumes qualification with the corrected command and unchanged
RC20 compiler bytes.

## [0.1.0-rc.20]

Twentieth candidate for `0.1.0`, prepared on 13 November 2026. It corrects
compiler bridge defects exposed during local qualification.
Qualification and publication remain pending in the live
[quality record](https://github.com/0x000000000000000000001/gopurs/blob/main/docs/quality-0.1.0.md).

### Fixed

- Convert curried callback values through the native FFI bridge instead of
  assuming that a foreign function is already a boxed runtime value.
- Consume the TAST arguments actually accepted by the Go implementation,
  including arguments of a returned function; preserve a function result when
  Go returns it. Add focused regressions for both bridge cases.
- Preserve the original TAST annotation at zero-argument Go wrappers' ignored
  `Unit` boundary, so `Unit -> Int` with Go `func() any` produces an `Int`
  rather than an extra function. Keep `Fn0` scalar and function results intact.
- Pin the Foreign port's safe readers for native Go strings, booleans, numbers
  and slices. Indexed reads recognize native slices; reading an array or a
  property preserves shared and cyclic native child values.

The frontend and other library pins remain those of RC19. The compiler changes
require a new benchmark and complete validation; the historical RC18 campaign
and its local RC19 equality proof do not qualify this candidate.

## [0.1.0-rc.19]

Nineteenth candidate for `0.1.0`, prepared on 13 November 2026, retaining
RC18's compiler, runtime and dependency pins. Qualification and publication
remain pending in the live
[quality record](https://github.com/0x000000000000000000001/gopurs/blob/main/docs/quality-0.1.0.md).

### Fixed

- Include the Aff and Foreign native preflight paths in the isolated library
  cleanup fixture. Stub these preflights consistently with the other library
  runners, preserving the requirement to reach the mock Spago command and the
  neighbor-cache sentinels. Allow the isolated subprocess to start its own
  Node test runner by removing the inherited test-runner context from its
  environment. The real library scripts and native suites remain unchanged;
  this corrects the test setup that stopped RC18 qualification.

## [0.1.0-rc.18]

Eighteenth candidate for `0.1.0`, retaining RC17's compiler and runtime.
Qualification and publication status remain in the live
[quality record](https://github.com/0x000000000000000000001/gopurs/blob/main/docs/quality-0.1.0.md).

### Fixed

- Refresh the Release and Dev `FFIIntegerReturns` snapshots for the ordinary
  FFI array conversion introduced in RC15. The references now use the runtime
  array accessors, matching the generated code already exercised successfully
  by the JavaScript and native hosts. Compiler and runtime behavior are unchanged.
- Select the Go Buffer port in the `node-net` and `node-streams` test
  configurations and generated locks. Their Release and Dev suites pass with
  this dependency selection; the bootstrap manifest pins the reviewed commits.
- Supply Spec's two missing node-child-process value helpers: an undefined
  sentinel distinct from null, and kill-signal dispatch matching the stock
  JavaScript number/string conversion. This supports Spec's test dependency,
  not the complete node-child-process API. Contract checks and the complete
  Release/Dev Spec suites cover the new source pin.
- Record the incomplete historical HTTP benchmark input separately from
  compiler qualification. Its reachable `stdout` foreign binding lacked a Go
  implementation; the current library port already supplies it. Historical
  inputs and measurements remain unchanged.

## [0.1.0-rc.17]

Seventeenth candidate for `0.1.0`, retaining RC16's ordinary Go FFI contract,
dependency pins and frontend build fixes. Qualification and publication status
remain in the [quality record](https://github.com/0x000000000000000000001/gopurs/blob/main/docs/quality-0.1.0.md).

### Fixed

- Emit missing-FFI annotations with identical JSON key order and string escaping
  on the JavaScript and native compiler hosts. The metadata keeps the same
  schema and decoded values; generated executable code is unchanged. A real
  batch-compilation regression checks byte identity and JSON round-tripping
  across hosts, including Unicode, quotes, backslashes and literal escapes.

## [0.1.0-rc.16]

Sixteenth candidate for `0.1.0`, retaining RC15's ordinary Go FFI, dependency
pins and compatibility scope. The [quality record](https://github.com/0x000000000000000000001/gopurs/blob/main/docs/quality-0.1.0.md)
tracks qualification and publication.

### Fixed

- Keep the selected typed and stock frontends rooted in Nix throughout CI and
  publication smoke tests, so garbage collection cannot remove them between
  build and execution.
- Correct the test domain in the Nix frontend dependency Foundation 0.0.30:
  integer division properties now exclude quotients that cannot be represented
  by their tested type, as well as division by zero. This prevents the
  reproducible `Int8 (-128) / (-1)` test overflow found during RC15 qualification.
  Foundation implementation code and test configuration are unchanged: Linux
  CI keeps the complete suite enabled; Darwin retains the pinned nixpkgs
  policy and was checked explicitly with the failing seed (6,121 tests).

## [0.1.0-rc.15]

Fifteenth experimental candidate for `0.1.0`. Its qualification and publication
status are recorded in the live [quality record](https://github.com/0x000000000000000000001/gopurs/blob/main/docs/quality-0.1.0.md)
and [release checklist](https://github.com/0x000000000000000000001/gopurs/blob/main/docs/release-checklist.md).
At preparation on 12 November 2026, RC14 was the published candidate on `next`
and `latest` selected RC7. Local FFI results do not qualify RC15's final artifacts.

### Added

- [Ordinary Go FFI](docs/ffi-idiomatic.md): native `Effect` and `EffectFnAff`
  results, Go errors, optional `context.Context`, typed callbacks, opaque
  handles and closed-record conversion to local Go structs. Generated adapters
  own the runtime integration; handwritten implementations can use Go tooling
  directly. Direct ordinary `Aff`, open-record layout inference and a general
  multi-constructor ADT mapping remain outside this contract.
- Focused parser, runtime race, documented-example, end-to-end and installed
  package regressions, including both compiler hosts, cold/warm caches,
  signature changes, rejection and recovery.

### Fixed

- Keep asynchronous operations lazy and repeatable, arbitrate completion and
  cancellation, and release failed or late acquisitions exactly once before
  ownership transfers. Callbacks retained by a Go service follow that service's
  explicit unsubscribe/close lifetime.
- Convert dynamic `Foreign` data without JSON round-trips; preserve native
  handles, nested containers, null and a distinct undefined marker. Functions
  and algebraic constructors still require an explicit PureScript conversion.
- Diagnose missing TAST metadata before optimization and incompatible expanded
  `EffectFn2`/`EffectFn3` results with frontend, `PATH` and clean-output guidance.
  Require nominal `EffectFnAff` metadata for its ordinary Go ABI; retain valid
  explicit callback implementations. Preserve valid cache state after an FFI
  signature error.
- Validate missing FFI in explicitly selected entry-point scopes, and retain
  the cleanup of build/test tooling and the separately pinned Argonaut codecs
  support checkout already integrated since RC14.

### Changed

- Pin the typed frontend to `ae6a6f644502bafcfa4fa94d8f81a1a1a1ca5080`,
  `gopurs-aff` to `dbe9ff1c574a18352cf9ec861090083b14ca0246`, and
  `gopurs-foreign` to `c79499d6c22fd0637104bec5449434cfb6e31fe4`.
  Rebuild frontend output after switching revisions, preserving application
  `go.mod` and `go.sum`; the `purs` version number alone does not identify the
  required TAST contract. Existing explicit runtime FFI remains supported.

## [0.1.0-rc.14]

Fourteenth candidate for `0.1.0`, with a deterministic spec timeout fixture
following RC13's macOS Dev failure. The exact signed tag passed qualification
on all three supported platforms and its artifacts were reviewed. Published on
npm `next` and as a GitHub prerelease; public Hello, b8x compilation/linking and
the real `next` rollback to RC7 followed by restoration to RC14 passed. `latest`
remains RC7. The embedded documentation deviation and rollback scope are recorded in [the quality report](https://github.com/0x000000000000000000001/gopurs/blob/main/docs/quality-0.1.0.md#rc14-qualification-and-artifact-review--5-november-2026).

### Fixed

- Pin `gopurs-spec` at `7bbb30f00bfde95cdb39286662bb5a0f71e3f368`
  ([spec PR #2](https://github.com/0x000000000000000000001/gopurs-spec/pull/2),
  reviewed and merged): replace the 15 ms body delay in the fail-fast timeout
  fixture with cancellable `never`, retaining the 10 ms timeout and golden
  output. Targeted local Dev and Release checks pass under CPU contention;
  they use a development toolchain and do not qualify this candidate.

Compiler/runtime, frontend, optimizer, all other source pins and CI workflows
are unchanged. RC13's tag and results remain unchanged.

## [0.1.0-rc.13]

Thirteenth candidate for `0.1.0`, correcting the CI input selector after RC12.
Compiler/runtime, frontend, optimizer, library pins and test corpus remain
unchanged. Qualification failed in macOS spec Dev: 73 passing, 3 pending and
one failing timeout fixture. Both Linux core jobs and macOS spec Release passed;
fixtures and finalization were skipped. RC13 remains unqualified and unpublished,
and its tag is immutable.

### Fixed

- Accept an aggregate GitHub run status of `queued` when selecting fixture,
  qualification or finalized inputs. Keep requiring the exact successful
  producer jobs, source and artifact identities, and signature checks.
  Pending or failed producers continue to block selection.

## [0.1.0-rc.12]

Twelfth candidate for `0.1.0`, correcting the Nix cache inventory check that
blocked RC11 before Linux quality tests. Compiler/runtime, frontend, optimizer,
library pins and test corpus remain unchanged. Three build/core jobs passed,
but nine fixture shards failed before import because the input selector
rejected the aggregate run status `queued`. The run subsequently completed
with failure. RC12 remains unqualified and unpublished; its signed tag is
immutable.

### Fixed

- Accept the empty `realisations` directory created by Nix 2.28.3 during a
  runtime-path cache export. Continue rejecting nonempty auxiliary directories,
  symlinks and unknown cache entries; no metadata is silently discarded.

## [0.1.0-rc.11]

Eleventh candidate for `0.1.0`, grouping CI recovery and documentation after
RC10's infrastructure failures. Compiler, runtime, TAST/frontend, optimizer
and library pins are unchanged. Both Linux jobs failed at the runtime-cache
export inventory check; RC11 remains unqualified and unpublished.

### Changed

- Reuse the build's exact locked Nix runtime environment in fixture shards,
  with bounded preparation and diagnostics, instead of rebuilding that
  environment in every shard.
- Retain the actual producer attempt for each qualification artifact so a
  targeted retry can reuse successful work from the same run and source.
  Exact compiler and toolchain identities remain required; historical tags
  and their qualification results are unchanged.

## [0.1.0-rc.10]

Tenth candidate for `0.1.0`, carrying the compiler/runtime and platform choices
of RC9 with the corrected spec source pin. Both qualification attempts failed
in environment/bootstrap preparation; the complete retry passed all three
builds and eleven fixture shards but timed out before the remaining shard's
tests. RC10 is unqualified and unpublished; RC7 remains public.

### Fixed

- Pin `gopurs-spec` at `c88da162df5d9ef85d672f5f2e819bb287e9647b`:
  await cancellation of compiler subprocesses and their process groups before
  reusing an integration directory; emit native child `close` only after
  stdout/stderr delivery and `exit`. Include native lifecycle and Aff
  cancellation regressions. Keep fixture source and golden output unchanged.
- Give a whole integration case, including cold compilation, a finite default
  budget of 300 seconds before parsing explicit timeout options. Log each
  preparation/runtime phase so future failures identify the expensive command.

Local corrected-source spec tests pass in Release and Dev (74 passing,
3 pending, all nine integration cases per profile). They use a development
frontend on macOS arm64 and do not replace this candidate's full qualification.

## [0.1.0-rc.9]

Ninth candidate for `0.1.0`, carrying the same compiler, runtime and dependency
pins as RC8. Qualification failed in the macOS spec integration tests; RC9
is unpublished and its tag remains immutable. RC7 remains public.

### Fixed

- Move both the macOS build and fixture jobs to the ARM64 `macos-15` runner.
  GitHub cancelled RC8's macOS job before any steps ran during the macOS 14
  retirement schedule. The new qualification does not establish compatibility
  with macOS 14. Keep the build and fixture runner matrices consistent through
  the CI policy regression test.

## [0.1.0-rc.8]

Eighth candidate for `0.1.0`, prepared from the post-RC7 fixes and reviewed
cleanup. Its macOS job was cancelled before any steps ran because GitHub
retired that runner image; the remaining campaign was cancelled. RC8 is
unqualified and unpublished. Its signed tag remains immutable, and RC7 remains
the published candidate.

The TAST frontend remains pinned to
`105f5752b39cc0f6c99a40064295338bf57ad223`, and the backend optimizer to
`4e7de48ffd6e19480ed3de6bfe8ca8227133be13`. The supported targets remain Linux
amd64/arm64 and macOS arm64. Rust stays experimental, and the documented
compatibility limits still apply. The existing benchmark record predates this
candidate; it does not establish RC8 performance results.

### Fixed

- Keep the original producer job and artifact attempt when GitHub copies a
  completed execution into retry metadata. Require matching execution evidence
  and keep newer failed or pending executions blocking recovery.
- Accept npm's absent-to-empty DSSE `keyid` serialization without changing
  signed payloads, signature bytes or cryptographic verification requirements.
- Pin the node-fs synchronous/asynchronous `chmod` and file stream fixes, the
  native node-streams pipe implementation, and the node-http/event-emitter
  response-body fixes. Preserve the targeted regressions and add the missing
  Go `stdout` adaptation used by the HTTP tests.
- Complete the identified uuid and js-bigints source metadata and attribution
  corrections without changing their library code or existing licenses.

### Changed

- Include all 51 pinned library suites through `bin/modtest` in future full
  release qualification, in Release and Dev profiles. Reuse the native compiler,
  trim the private Go cache between libraries, retain campaign reports and logs,
  and require exact library revisions and complete coverage before finalization.
  Ordinary quick CI and existing release tags keep their current scope.
- Replace external HTTP test endpoints with a local HTTPS fixture, retaining
  certificate verification and refusal tests. Remove the unused `go get`
  resolution of `strcase` from strings-extra.
- Derive the optional quick-CI frontend cache key from its Nix derivation and
  platform. Full candidate qualification continues to bypass this cache.
- Group compiler host services under `Gopurs.Host`, move the embedded runtime
  source under `Gopurs.Runtime.Source`, and document the module map and naming.
  Add output-identity and documentation checks; quick receipts now require all
  24 gates under `linux-quick-v2`. Check test inventories before CI builds.

The next candidate must validate its own exact artifacts, 371 gates per
platform (including 51 libraries and 401 fixtures in each profile), signatures
and installation. Historical RC7 and local post-RC7 results remain supporting
evidence only; they do not close those candidate gates. RC7 reinstallation has
been checked locally, but application suitability and public rollback remain
open in the release checklist.

## [0.1.0-rc.7]

Seventh candidate for `0.1.0`. RC6 was not published: its Linux amd64 core
campaign exposed an intermittent asynchronous emission failure. The macOS and
Linux arm64 core jobs passed; fixture shards did not run. Earlier tags remain
immutable.

### Fixed

- Return pipelined worker failures as explicit results and propagate them at
  dependency joins and producer boundaries. A worker error no longer escapes
  globally while its producer is suspended, including under supervision.
  Failures remain sticky and prevent queued dependent batches from starting.
- Include emission lifecycle regression tests in quick PR qualification.
- Retry signing and draft upload using the exact successful qualification of
  the same immutable tag, preserving the original test and compiler identities.
- Use pinned Node directly for finalization, avoiding a redundant Nix setup,
  and balance Release/Dev batches across the four existing fixture shards.

## [0.1.0-rc.6]

Sixth candidate for `0.1.0`, with the compiler and dependency pins of RC5.
RC5 passed all three core jobs and all twelve fixture shards, but final
attestation failed. It was not published; its signed tag remains immutable.

### Fixed

- Add a reproducible UUID serial number to the CycloneDX dependency inventory,
  required by the GitHub attestation action.
- Recover an existing Rekor entry when the signing service accepted a request
  but its retry returned HTTP 409. Continue to verify the complete signature,
  transparency-log proof, artifact digest and GitHub workflow identity before
  accepting the recovered entry.
- Publish using the CI provenance bundle already verified for the candidate,
  preserving the same attestation for publication recovery.

## [0.1.0-rc.5]

Fifth candidate for `0.1.0`, retaining the compiler, dependencies and feature
scope of RC4. RC4 was not published: all three core jobs and ten fixture shards
passed, but a Linux runner lost communication and two macOS fixtures could not
start Spago (`ENOENT`). The signed RC4 tag remains immutable.

### Changed

- Keep CI development tools reachable through a persistent Nix profile for the
  lifetime of each job. This adds an explicit garbage-collection root instead
  of relying on platform-dependent process inspection. Garbage collection has
  not been established as the cause of the RC4 macOS failure.
- Include the working directory and searched executable paths, with existence
  checks, when a fixture command cannot start. Preserve the original failure;
  do not silently retry or skip it.

## [0.1.0-rc.4]

Fourth candidate for `0.1.0`, retaining the compiler, pinned dependencies,
features and limitations below. RC3 was not published: all three build/core
jobs passed, but fixture qualification failed. A local reproduction exposed a
race while initializing Spago's shared registry cache. The previous signed
candidate tags remain immutable.

### Fixed

- Initialize fixture dependencies once with `spago fetch` before starting
  parallel batches on a fresh runner. Keep fresh fixture workspaces, both build
  profiles, the existing resource limits and all 401 fixtures per profile.
- Preserve Spago diagnostics on a failed fixture by removing its quiet flag.
- Reuse qualified PR results after merge even when GitHub clears the run's PR
  association list, while checking the actual tested tree, parents, receipt,
  repository, run and artifact identity.
- Import cached frontend tools using their complete Nix store paths and verify
  the imported paths before recording success.

### Changed

- Run ordinary PR checks on Linux amd64 and skip heavy builds for documentation
  changes. Tags and explicit full campaigns retain all three supported targets.
- Cache the pinned frontend runtime closure for quick runs; missing or unusable
  cache entries fall back to a fresh build. Full release runs remain independent
  of this cache.
- Align active public installation examples and candidate tables with this
  version, and check tag/package/lockfile/changelog agreement before heavy builds.

## [0.1.0-rc.3]

Third candidate for `0.1.0`, retaining the compiler, pinned dependencies,
features and limitations of the candidates below. RC2 was not published:
its Linux core gates passed, but the checkout action replaced the local
annotated tag with its peeled commit and artifact preparation rejected it.
The signed RC1 and RC2 tags are retained.

### Fixed

- Select release tags explicitly in every CI checkout, preserving their
  annotated objects while retaining the default commit selection for PRs.
- Check source commit and annotated tag identity immediately after checkout.
  Verify that the local tag object matches GitHub's verified signature before
  starting the release build.

## [0.1.0-rc.2]

Second candidate for `0.1.0`, retaining the frontend, bootstrap dependencies,
features and known limitations listed for `0.1.0-rc.1` below. The first candidate
was not published to npm or GitHub Releases: its full macOS gate timed out while
compiling the native scanner test, and both Linux jobs reached their six-hour
limit during the fixture campaign. The signed first-candidate tag is retained.

### Fixed

- Compile the native scanner, preparation and emission functional probes without
  Go optimizations for their large compiler package, keeping the existing memory
  budget, assertions, execution deadlines, scanner stack limit and race checks.
  Release compiler binaries retain their optimized bootstrap profile.
- Include the scanner and preparation probes in the quick CI campaign so their
  compilation and execution are checked before creating another release tag.
- Publish build manifests, FFI digests and global-function sidecars from each
  cache session's private stage. Concurrent builds no longer share a temporary
  sidecar path that another writer can rename, causing an `ENOENT` failure.
- Separate full CI into core checks and four fixture shards per platform,
  reusing the exact candidate compiler. Require complete Release/Dev coverage
  and matching source, compiler and run identities before signing artifacts.
- Upload stable quality logs and reports instead of live generated workspaces,
  avoiding missing-file errors while interrupted processes clean up temporary
  compiler snapshots.

## [0.1.0-rc.1]

First release candidate for `0.1.0`, using the typed PureScript compiler at
`105f5752b39cc0f6c99a40064295338bf57ad223` and the bootstrap libraries pinned in
`bootstrap-sources.json`. The [qualification record](https://github.com/0x000000000000000000001/gopurs/blob/main/docs/quality-0.1.0.md)
distinguishes completed local checks from the remaining tag and public-install
gates. The [benchmark protocol](https://github.com/0x000000000000000000001/gopurs/blob/main/docs/release-benchmark.md) defines the cold and
warm measurements; the historical reference is the official altbak.pub table.

### Added

- First public release candidate preparation for `0.1.0`.
- PureScript-to-Go backend driven by typed TAST.
- JavaScript, native Go and experimental Rust compiler hosts.
- Content-verified incremental cache and optional Go package layout.
- Go runtime, FFI bridge and event loop.
- Compiler bootstrap documentation, checksums and clean-install checks.
- Publication scope, limitations, migration, CLI, quickstart and troubleshooting
  documentation.
- npm package allowlist and package-surface check.
- CI for Linux arm64/amd64 and macOS arm64.
- Nix packages, apps, development shell and application checks with pinned
  frontend, Node.js and Go toolchains.
- Public, commit-pinned bootstrap library inventory and `bin/setup --locked`.
- Versioned Argonaut codec adaptation for the native bootstrap.

### Fixed

- Go `int32` FFI arguments and results preserve signed integer values through
  scalar, array and callback bridges instead of falling through to pointer
  unboxing.

- The private output-barrier cache test now copies the `c1c` module resolved by
  `build-cache/go.mod`.
- Cache transition tests pin the monolithic layout and disable pack publication
  when they inspect individual cache objects.
- The context-transition check accounts for prepared fingerprints that are
  legitimately reused within a run.

### Known limitations

- The backend remains experimental and is not a drop-in replacement for the
  upstream PureScript compiler.
- The typed compiler fork and Go library ports are separate prerequisites.
- Stock PureScript libraries expose JavaScript FFI and may fail at runtime when
  a foreign declaration is reached.
- Windows, 32-bit targets, daemon/resident modes and the Rust host are outside
  the `0.1.x` production contract.
- Performance figures are measurements, not guarantees.

### Security

- No public security release has been made yet. See `SECURITY.md`.

module Gopurs.AffineLoops (wrap, globalTarget, localTarget) where

import Prelude

import Control.Alternative (guard)
import Data.Array as Array
import Data.Array.NonEmpty as NEA
import Data.Foldable (any, foldl)
import Data.Map as Map
import Data.Maybe (Maybe(..))
import Data.Newtype (unwrap)
import Data.String as String
import Data.Tuple (Tuple(..))
import Gopurs.ExprContext (ExprContext, LocalEnv, TranslateExpr, childContext, flattenStmts)
import Gopurs.FilteredSumLoops as FilteredSumLoops
import Gopurs.GoAst (GoExpr(..), GoType(..), sanitizeName)
import Gopurs.GoFunctions (Parameters)
import Gopurs.RecordAffineLoops as RecordAffineLoops
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.Codegen.Tco (TcoExpr(..))
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.CoreFn (Ident(..), Literal(..), Qualified(..))
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.FreeVars (localId)
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.Syntax (BackendSyntax, Pair(..))
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.Syntax as Syn

type Recurrence = { counter :: String, accumulator :: String, increment :: Int, reads :: Array TcoExpr }

-- Match the complete pure recurrence before changing its execution count. The
-- original loop remains the fallback for zero, negative and wide entry values.
-- Unused global reads retain their first demand in source order. Generated
-- PureScript getters memoize initialization; foreign getters return a binding
-- materialized at package initialization (Printer/FfiBridge). Reading a Var
-- never invokes the function or Effect it may contain. Calls, accessors,
-- callbacks and effects are not admitted as reads.
wrap :: TranslateExpr -> ExprContext -> (TcoExpr -> Boolean) -> Parameters -> GoType -> TcoExpr -> GoExpr -> GoExpr
wrap translate context self params result body original = case recognize self params body of
  Just recurrence | result == TypeInt64 ->
    let
      counter = GoVar (recurrence.counter <> "_loop")
      accumulator = GoVar (recurrence.accumulator <> "_loop")
      positive = GoBinOp ">" counter (integer 0)
      bounded = GoBinOp "<=" counter (integer top)
      signed = GoBinOp "==" accumulator (cast "int64" (cast "int32" accumulator))
      admitted = GoBinOp "&&" (GoBinOp "&&" positive bounded) signed
      -- Both factors are signed 32-bit, with a positive counter. Their product
      -- plus the signed accumulator fits int64. IntMul intentionally has JS
      -- Number rounding semantics, so it cannot implement this exact sum.
      total = GoBinOp "+" accumulator (GoBinOp "*" counter (integer recurrence.increment))
      value = cast "int64" (cast "int32" total)
    in GoBlock [ GoIfElse admitted (emitReads translate context recurrence.reads <> [ GoReturn value ]) [], original ]
  _ -> RecordAffineLoops.wrap self params result body
    (FilteredSumLoops.wrap self params result body original)

recognize :: (TcoExpr -> Boolean) -> Parameters -> TcoExpr -> Maybe Recurrence
recognize self params body = do
  Tuple first second <- case params of
    [ Tuple first TypeInt64, Tuple second TypeInt64 ] | first /= second -> Just (Tuple first second)
    _ -> Nothing
  branch <- case syntax body of
    Syn.Branch branches step -> case NEA.toArray branches of
      [ Pair condition seed ] -> Just { condition, seed, step }
      _ -> Nothing
    _ -> Nothing
  counter <- case syntax branch.condition of
    Syn.PrimOp (Syn.Op2 (Syn.OpIntOrd Syn.OpEq) left right)
      | literal 0 right -> localName left
      | literal 0 left -> localName right
    _ -> Nothing
  guard (counter == first || counter == second)
  let accumulator = if counter == first then second else first
  guard (local accumulator branch.seed)
  prefix <- strictReads 64 branch.step
  args <- case syntax prefix.body of
    Syn.App target args | self target -> Just (NEA.toArray args)
    Syn.UncurriedApp target args | self target -> Just args
    _ -> Nothing
  Tuple nextCounter nextAccumulator <- case args of
    [ a, b ] -> Just (if counter == first then Tuple a b else Tuple b a)
    _ -> Nothing
  guard (case syntax nextCounter of
    Syn.PrimOp (Syn.Op2 (Syn.OpIntNum Syn.OpSubtract) left right) -> local counter left && literal 1 right
    _ -> false)
  constant <- case syntax nextAccumulator of
    Syn.PrimOp (Syn.Op2 (Syn.OpIntNum Syn.OpAdd) left right)
      | local accumulator left -> Just right
      | local accumulator right -> Just left
    _ -> Nothing
  -- Closed scalar evaluation may retain strict reads inside the constant
  -- operand. The other operand and counter update are already proven pure;
  -- these demands therefore follow the step prefix in either argument order.
  suffix <- strictReads (64 - Array.length prefix.reads) constant
  increment <- intLiteral suffix.body
  guard (increment >= bottom && increment <= top)
  pure { counter, accumulator, increment, reads: prefix.reads <> suffix.reads }

-- Match the whole suffix, including every local level, before discarding a
-- binding. Locals, projections and arbitrary initializers keep the old loop.
strictReads :: Int -> TcoExpr -> Maybe { reads :: Array TcoExpr, body :: TcoExpr }
strictReads remaining expression = case syntax expression of
  Syn.Let ident level value body -> do
    guard (remaining > 0)
    case syntax value of
      Syn.Var _ -> pure unit
      _ -> Nothing
    guard (not (usesLocal ident level body))
    suffix <- strictReads (remaining - 1) body
    pure { reads: Array.cons value suffix.reads, body: suffix.body }
  _ -> Just { reads: [], body: expression }

usesLocal :: Maybe Ident -> Syn.Level -> TcoExpr -> Boolean
usesLocal ident level (TcoExpr _ value) = case value of
  Syn.Local name at -> ident == name && level == at
  _ -> any (usesLocal ident level) value

-- Translate each demand normally so its representation and any strict
-- conversion remain intact. Never inherit the recurrence's Int result type.
emitReads :: TranslateExpr -> ExprContext -> Array TcoExpr -> Array GoExpr
emitReads translate context values =
  (foldl emit { next: 0, statements: [] } values).statements
  where
  emit acc value =
    let result = translate (childContext context Nothing) acc.next value
    in { next: result.nextId
       , statements: acc.statements <> flattenStmts result.stmts <> [ GoMutate "_" result.expr ]
       }

syntax :: TcoExpr -> BackendSyntax TcoExpr
syntax (TcoExpr _ value) = case value of
  Syn.Typed _ inner -> syntax inner
  _ -> value

localName :: TcoExpr -> Maybe String
localName expr = case syntax expr of
  Syn.Local ident level -> Just (localId ident level)
  _ -> Nothing

local :: String -> TcoExpr -> Boolean
local name expr = localName expr == Just name

intLiteral :: TcoExpr -> Maybe Int
intLiteral expr = case syntax expr of
  Syn.Lit (LitInt value) -> Just value
  _ -> Nothing

literal :: Int -> TcoExpr -> Boolean
literal value expr = intLiteral expr == Just value

globalTarget :: String -> String -> TcoExpr -> Boolean
globalTarget moduleName name expr = case syntax expr of
  Syn.Var (Qualified (Just owner) (Ident ident)) ->
    String.replaceAll (String.Pattern ".") (String.Replacement "_") (unwrap owner) == moduleName
      && sanitizeName ident == name
  _ -> false

localTarget :: LocalEnv -> String -> TcoExpr -> Boolean
localTarget bound name expr = case localName expr >>= flip Map.lookup bound of
  Just binding -> binding.name == name
  Nothing -> false

cast :: String -> GoExpr -> GoExpr
cast name value = GoCall (GoVar name) [ value ]

integer :: Int -> GoExpr
integer = cast "int64" <<< GoInt

module Gopurs.BindingExprs
  ( nonRecursive
  , recursive
  ) where

import Prelude
import Data.Array as Array
import Data.Array.NonEmpty (NonEmptyArray, toArray)
import Data.Foldable (foldMap, foldl)
import Data.Map as Map
import Data.Maybe (Maybe(..), fromMaybe)
import Data.Newtype (unwrap)
import Data.Traversable (traverse)
import Data.Tuple (Tuple(..), fst, snd)
import Effect.Ref as Ref
import Effect.Unsafe (unsafePerformEffect)
import Gopurs.CallAnalysis (extractUncurriedAbs)
import Gopurs.ExprAnalysis (extractExprFuncType, functionResultAfter, getExprType, printTcoExprShape, unwrapTcoExpr)
import Gopurs.ExprContext (ExprContext, ExprResult, LocalEnv, TranslateExpr, StmtTree(..), bindParameters, childContext)
import Gopurs.GoAst (rawGo, GoExpr(..), GoType(..), goTypeToStr, sanitizeName)
import Gopurs.GoConversions (coerceGoExpr)
import Gopurs.GoTypes (exprTypeToGoType, isCompositeGoType, printExprType)
import Gopurs.GoFunctions (loopParameters)
import Gopurs.LocalWorkers as LocalWorkers
import Gopurs.ImmediateFfiEffects as ImmediateFfiEffects
import Gopurs.Printer (printGoExpr)
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.Codegen.Tco (TcoExpr(..))
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.CoreFn (Ident(..))
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.FreeVars (localId)
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.Syntax (BackendSyntax(Local), Level)

nonRecursive :: TranslateExpr -> ExprContext -> Int -> Maybe Ident -> Level -> TcoExpr -> TcoExpr -> ExprResult
nonRecursive translate context nextId mbIdent lvl binding body =
  case ImmediateFfiEffects.translate translate context nextId mbIdent lvl binding body of
    Just result -> result
    Nothing -> nonRecursiveBinding translate context nextId mbIdent lvl binding body

nonRecursiveBinding :: TranslateExpr -> ExprContext -> Int -> Maybe Ident -> Level -> TcoExpr -> TcoExpr -> ExprResult
nonRecursiveBinding translate context@{ metadata, codegenStateRef, depth, modNameStr, moduleFunctions, bound } nextId mbIdent lvl binding body =
  let
    originalName = localId mbIdent lvl
    name = originalName <> "_" <> show nextId
    expectedGoTypeFromAst = exprTypeToGoType metadata.sharedRecords metadata.pointerAdtPaths metadata.enumAdts metadata.elidedCtors modNameStr (getExprType binding)

    mbFunc = extractUncurriedAbs binding
  in
    case mbFunc of
      Just abs | Array.length abs.args > 0 ->
        let
          params = LocalWorkers.parameters context abs.args binding
          loopBound = bindParameters params bound
          resBodyMut = translate (context { depth = (depth + 1), bound = loopBound, tcoIdent = (Just name), loopCtx = [], options = { isTail: true, inEffectBlock: false }, mbExpectedExprType = Nothing, mbExpectedGoType = Nothing }) (nextId + 1) abs.body
          -- The binding is non-recursive: infer its native result before
          -- publishing the signature to callers. Only its curried wrapper
          -- crosses the Value boundary, which can otherwise copy whole lists.
          trueFRet = resBodyMut.exprType
          localModuleFunctions = Map.insert name (LocalWorkers.signature context name params trueFRet) moduleFunctions
          keepWrapper = LocalWorkers.needsWrapper originalName (Array.length params) body
          worker = LocalWorkers.emit translate context name params keepWrapper Nothing resBodyMut

          newBound = Map.insert originalName { name, goType: TypeValue } bound
          resBodyOuter = translate (context { depth = (depth + 1), moduleFunctions = localModuleFunctions, bound = newBound, tcoIdent = Nothing, mbExpectedExprType = Nothing }) resBodyMut.nextId body
        in
          { stmts: foldMap StmtLeaf (worker.declarations <> worker.assignments) <> resBodyOuter.stmts, expr: resBodyOuter.expr, exprType: resBodyOuter.exprType, nextId: resBodyOuter.nextId }

      _ ->
        let
          -- An identity continuation consumes this binding as the enclosing
          -- result. Propagate only that concrete ABI, never an unrelated
          -- parent's expectation into arbitrary let-bound computations.
          bindingExpected = case unwrapTcoExpr body of
            Local bodyIdent bodyLevel | bodyIdent == mbIdent && bodyLevel == lvl -> context.mbExpectedGoType
            _ -> Nothing
          resBinding = translate (context { depth = (depth + 1), tcoIdent = Nothing, loopCtx = [], options = { isTail: false, inEffectBlock: false }, mbExpectedExprType = Nothing, mbExpectedGoType = bindingExpected }) (nextId + 1) binding
          -- Keep a composite producer's boxed representation across the let.
          -- Native consumers adapt their own arguments; generic consumers and
          -- captured callbacks can reuse the immutable value directly.
          actualGoType = fromMaybe
            ( if expectedGoTypeFromAst == TypeValue
                || (resBinding.exprType == TypeValue && isCompositeGoType expectedGoTypeFromAst)
              then resBinding.exprType
              else expectedGoTypeFromAst
            )
            bindingExpected
          newBound = Map.insert originalName { name, goType: actualGoType } bound
          resBody = translate (context { depth = (depth + 1), bound = newBound, tcoIdent = Nothing }) resBinding.nextId body
          letStmt =
            if actualGoType == resBinding.exprType then
              StmtLeaf (GoAssign name resBinding.expr)
            else
              StmtLeaf (rawGo ("var " <> name <> " " <> goTypeToStr actualGoType <> " = " <> printGoExpr (coerceGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr resBinding.expr resBinding.exprType actualGoType)))
        in
          { stmts: resBinding.stmts <> StmtLeaf (rawGo ("// TAST (Let): " <> name <> " shape=" <> printTcoExprShape binding <> " bindingType=" <> printExprType (getExprType binding))) <> letStmt <> resBody.stmts, expr: resBody.expr, exprType: resBody.exprType, nextId: resBody.nextId }

recursive :: TranslateExpr -> ExprContext -> Int -> TcoExpr -> Level -> NonEmptyArray (Tuple Ident TcoExpr) -> TcoExpr -> ExprResult
recursive translate context@{ metadata, depth, modNameStr, recVars, moduleFunctions } nextId (TcoExpr tcoAnalysis _) lvl bindings body =
  let
    allocated = allocateRecursive context nextId lvl (toArray bindings)
    combinedRecVars = recVars <> map (\(Tuple (Ident i) _) -> sanitizeName i) (toArray bindings)

    isLoop = (unwrap tcoAnalysis).role.isLoop
    mutRecBinds =
      if isLoop then
        traverse (\(Tuple (Ident name) val) -> map (\abs -> { ident: sanitizeName name, args: abs.args, body: abs.body, val }) (extractUncurriedAbs val)) (toArray bindings)
      else Nothing
  in
    case mutRecBinds of
      Just fns ->
        let
          -- Resolve parameters once, then publish every provisional signature
          -- before translating any body. The annotated return is provisional:
          -- bodies refine the function table in source order.
          workers = map
            ( \fn ->
                let
                  oldName = localId (Just (Ident fn.ident)) lvl
                  boundInfo = fromMaybe { name: oldName, goType: TypeValue } (Map.lookup oldName allocated.newBound)
                  newName = boundInfo.name
                  params = LocalWorkers.parameters context fn.args fn.val
                  -- The annotation flattens function-valued results into its
                  -- argument list. Only consume the worker's actual binders:
                  -- a recursive lookup may return a function still to apply.
                  expectedReturn = map (functionResultAfter (Array.length fn.args)) (extractExprFuncType (getExprType fn.val))
                  resultType = case expectedReturn of
                    Just ty -> exprTypeToGoType metadata.sharedRecords metadata.pointerAdtPaths metadata.enumAdts metadata.elidedCtors modNameStr ty
                    Nothing -> TypeValue
                in
                  { oldName, newName, params, expectedReturn, resultType, body: fn.body }
            )
            fns
          published = foldl
            (\acc worker ->
              { functions: Map.insert worker.newName (LocalWorkers.signature context worker.newName worker.params worker.resultType) acc.functions
              -- The local value is the boxed curried wrapper. Saturated calls
              -- obtain the native ABI from the separate function table.
              , bound: Map.insert worker.oldName { name: worker.newName, goType: TypeValue } acc.bound
              })
            { functions: moduleFunctions, bound: allocated.newBound }
            workers

          translatedWorkers = foldl
            ( \acc worker ->
                let
                  { oldName, newName, params } = worker
                  currentLoopCtx = [ { ident: newName, loopParams: map fst (loopParameters params), goTypes: map snd params } ]
                  -- Peer bindings keep the provisional view; only the function
                  -- table sees results inferred for earlier bodies in the group.
                  loopBound = bindParameters params published.bound
                  resBodyMut = translate (context { depth = (depth + 1), recVars = combinedRecVars, moduleFunctions = acc.moduleFunctions, bound = loopBound, tcoIdent = (Just newName), loopCtx = currentLoopCtx, options = { isTail: true, inEffectBlock: false }, mbExpectedExprType = worker.expectedReturn, mbExpectedGoType = Just worker.resultType }) acc.nextId worker.body
                  trueFRet = resBodyMut.exprType
                  keepWrapper = LocalWorkers.needsWrapper oldName (Array.length params) body
                    || Array.any (\(Tuple _ binding) -> LocalWorkers.needsWrapper oldName (Array.length params) binding) (toArray bindings)
                  emitted = LocalWorkers.emit translate (context { bound = published.bound }) newName params keepWrapper (Just worker.body) resBodyMut
                  newFunctions = Map.insert newName (LocalWorkers.signature context newName params trueFRet) acc.moduleFunctions
                  newBound2 = Map.insert oldName { name: newName, goType: TypeValue } acc.newBound
                in
                  { declarations: acc.declarations <> emitted.declarations, stmts: acc.stmts <> emitted.assignments, nextId: resBodyMut.nextId, moduleFunctions: newFunctions, newBound: newBound2 }
            )
            { declarations: [], stmts: [], nextId: allocated.nextId, moduleFunctions: published.functions, newBound: published.bound }
            workers

          resBodyOuter = translate (context { depth = (depth + 1), recVars = combinedRecVars, moduleFunctions = translatedWorkers.moduleFunctions, bound = translatedWorkers.newBound, tcoIdent = Nothing, mbExpectedExprType = Nothing }) translatedWorkers.nextId body
        in
          -- Every function in the recursive group must be in scope
          -- before emitting bodies that can refer to its peers.
          { stmts: foldMap StmtLeaf (translatedWorkers.declarations <> translatedWorkers.stmts) <> resBodyOuter.stmts, expr: resBodyOuter.expr, exprType: resBodyOuter.exprType, nextId: resBodyOuter.nextId }

      Nothing ->
        initializeRecursiveValues translate (context { recVars = combinedRecVars }) isLoop allocated (toArray bindings) body

type RecursiveAllocation =
  { newBound :: LocalEnv
  , newNames :: Array { oldName :: String, newName :: String }
  , nextId :: Int
  }

-- Reserve both local and module-wide identifiers before inspecting the group.
-- Every initializer receives the same complete set of renamed bindings.
allocateRecursive :: ExprContext -> Int -> Level -> Array (Tuple Ident TcoExpr) -> RecursiveAllocation
allocateRecursive { metadata, codegenStateRef, modNameStr, bound } nextId lvl =
  foldl
    (\acc (Tuple ident value) ->
      let
        oldName = localId (Just ident) lvl
        globalId = unsafePerformEffect do
          state <- Ref.read codegenStateRef
          Ref.modify_ (\current -> current { globalId = current.globalId + 1 }) codegenStateRef
          pure state.globalId
        newName = oldName <> "_" <> show acc.nextId <> "_" <> show globalId
        goType = exprTypeToGoType metadata.sharedRecords metadata.pointerAdtPaths metadata.enumAdts metadata.elidedCtors modNameStr (getExprType value)
      in
        { newBound: Map.insert oldName { name: newName, goType } acc.newBound
        , newNames: Array.snoc acc.newNames { oldName, newName }
        , nextId: acc.nextId + 1
        })
    { newBound: bound, newNames: [], nextId }

-- An early read must not observe Go's zero value. Initializers and the closures
-- they create read through cells; publish each pointer only after its complete
-- initializer and coercion. The enclosing body uses the initialized values.
initializeRecursiveValues :: TranslateExpr -> ExprContext -> Boolean -> RecursiveAllocation -> Array (Tuple Ident TcoExpr) -> TcoExpr -> ExprResult
initializeRecursiveValues translate context@{ codegenStateRef, modNameStr, depth } isLoop allocated bindings body =
  let
    initializingBound = foldl
      (\acc name -> Map.update (\binding -> Just (binding { name = "(*" <> name.newName <> "_cell)" })) name.oldName acc)
      allocated.newBound allocated.newNames
    initialized = foldl
      (\acc (Tuple (Tuple _ value) name) ->
        let
          valueResult = translate ((childContext context Nothing) { bound = initializingBound }) acc.nextId value
          expected = (fromMaybe { name: name.newName, goType: TypeValue } (Map.lookup name.oldName allocated.newBound)).goType
          assigned = coerceGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr valueResult.expr valueResult.exprType expected
        in
          { stmts: acc.stmts <> valueResult.stmts
              <> StmtLeaf (GoMutate name.newName assigned)
              <> StmtLeaf (GoMutate (name.newName <> "_cell") (rawGo ("&" <> name.newName)))
          , values: Array.snoc acc.values { name: name.newName, goType: expected }
          , nextId: valueResult.nextId
          })
      { stmts: StmtEmpty, values: [], nextId: allocated.nextId }
      (Array.zip bindings allocated.newNames)
    declarations = map (\value -> rawGo ("var " <> value.name <> " " <> goTypeToStr value.goType <> "\n_ = " <> value.name
      <> "\nvar " <> value.name <> "_cell *" <> goTypeToStr value.goType <> "\n_ = " <> value.name <> "_cell"
      <> "\n// FALLBACK TCO: isLoop=" <> show isLoop <> " len=" <> show (Array.length bindings))) initialized.values
    result = translate (context { depth = depth + 1, bound = allocated.newBound, tcoIdent = Nothing }) initialized.nextId body
  in
    { stmts: foldMap StmtLeaf declarations <> initialized.stmts <> result.stmts, expr: result.expr, exprType: result.exprType, nextId: result.nextId }

module Gopurs.LocalWorkers
  ( parameters
  , signature
  , needsWrapper
  , emit
  ) where

import Prelude
import Data.Array as Array
import Data.Foldable (any)
import Data.Maybe (Maybe(..))
import Data.String as String
import Data.Tuple (Tuple(..), snd)
import Gopurs.CodegenState (FunctionInfo)
import Gopurs.CallAnalysis (collectGoSpine, getGoSpineArgs)
import Gopurs.ExprAnalysis (extractExprFuncType, getExprType, unwrapTcoExpr)
import Gopurs.ExprContext (ExprContext, ExprResult, TranslateExpr, flattenStmts)
import Gopurs.GoAst (GoExpr(..), GoType(..), goTypeToStr, rawGo)
import Gopurs.GoSymbol (GoReference(..))
import Gopurs.GoConversions (boxGoExpr, coerceGoExpr)
import Gopurs.GoFunctions (Parameters, curriedFunction, iterationBindings, loopParameters, namedParameters)
import Gopurs.Int32Loops as Int32Loops
import Gopurs.AffineLoops as AffineLoops
import Gopurs.GoTypes (exprTypeToGoType)
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.Codegen.Tco (TcoExpr)
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.FreeVars (localId)
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.Syntax (BackendSyntax(App, Local))

-- Local workers use annotation slots directly. Module workers have a separate
-- ABI policy, including read-only record projections and native sum results.
parameters :: ExprContext -> Array String -> TcoExpr -> Parameters
parameters { metadata, modNameStr } names value =
  let
    types = case extractExprFuncType (getExprType value) of
      Just { fArgs } -> map (exprTypeToGoType metadata.sharedRecords metadata.pointerAdtPaths metadata.enumAdts metadata.elidedCtors modNameStr) fArgs
      Nothing -> []
  in
    namedParameters names types

workerName :: String -> String -> String
workerName modName name = "Call_local_" <> modName <> "_" <> name

signature :: ExprContext -> String -> Parameters -> GoType -> FunctionInfo
signature { modNameStr } name params result =
  { reference: LocalReference (workerName modNameStr name), fArgs: map snd params, fRet: result, arity: Array.length params }

-- Inspect the current TCO expression, not usage annotations from an earlier
-- IR. Saturated curried calls use the published native worker directly.
-- Every other occurrence keeps the wrapper, including partial applications,
-- returned functions, callback arguments and uses in peer closures.
needsWrapper :: String -> Int -> TcoExpr -> Boolean
needsWrapper target arity expression =
  let
    visit = needsWrapper target arity
    syntax = unwrapTcoExpr expression
  in case syntax of
    Local ident level -> localId ident level == target
    App _ _ ->
      let
        Tuple fn spine = collectGoSpine expression
        args = getGoSpineArgs spine
      in case unwrapTcoExpr fn of
        Local ident level | localId ident level == target && arity > 0 && Array.length args >= arity && onlyCurriedApplications expression -> any visit args
        _ -> any visit syntax
    _ -> any visit syntax

-- collectGoSpine also flattens uncurried applications. Keep their wrappers,
-- including when an uncurried application is nested under a curried one.
onlyCurriedApplications :: TcoExpr -> Boolean
onlyCurriedApplications expression = case unwrapTcoExpr expression of
  App fn _ -> onlyCurriedApplications fn
  Local _ _ -> true
  _ -> false

-- The translated body determines the native result. Only the curried wrapper
-- crosses Value. Declarations stay separate so recursive callers can place the
-- whole group's declarations before any assignment captures a peer worker.
emit :: TranslateExpr -> ExprContext -> String -> Parameters -> Boolean -> Maybe TcoExpr -> ExprResult -> { declarations :: Array GoExpr, assignments :: Array GoExpr }
emit translate context@{ codegenStateRef, modNameStr, bound } name params keepWrapper loopBody result =
  let
    nativeName = workerName modNameStr name
    resultType = result.exprType
    declarations =
      [ rawGo ("var " <> nativeName <> " func(" <> String.joinWith ", " (map (goTypeToStr <<< snd) params) <> ") " <> goTypeToStr resultType)
      , rawGo ("_ = " <> nativeName)
      ]
        <> if keepWrapper then
          [ rawGo ("var " <> name <> " gopurs_runtime.Value")
          , rawGo ("_ = " <> name)
          ]
        else []
    body = flattenStmts result.stmts <> [ GoReturn result.expr ]
    functionBody = case loopBody of
      Just source -> AffineLoops.wrap translate context (AffineLoops.localTarget bound name) params resultType source
        (Int32Loops.loop name params resultType body)
      Nothing -> GoBlock (iterationBindings params <> body)
    nativeAssignment = GoMutate nativeName (GoFuncBlock (loopParameters params) [ functionBody ] resultType)
    call = GoCall (GoVar nativeName) (map (\(Tuple param ty) ->
      coerceGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr (GoVar (param <> "_loop_val")) TypeValue ty) params)
    boxedResult = boxGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr call resultType
    wrapper = if Array.null params then
      curriedFunction [ Tuple "_" TypeValue ] TypeValue (GoBlock [ GoReturn boxedResult ])
      else Array.foldr (\(Tuple param _) inner ->
        GoCall (GoSelector (GoVar "gopurs_runtime") "Func")
          [ GoFuncLit [ Tuple (param <> "_loop_val") TypeValue ] [] inner TypeValue ]) boxedResult params
  in
    { declarations, assignments: [ nativeAssignment ] <> if keepWrapper then [ GoMutate name wrapper ] else [] }

module Gopurs.ModuleWorkers (declaration) where

import Prelude
import Data.Array as Array
import Data.Map as Map
import Data.Maybe (Maybe(..))
import Data.Tuple (Tuple(..), fst, snd)
import Effect.Ref as Ref
import Effect.Unsafe (unsafePerformEffect)
import Gopurs.ExprAnalysis (extractExprFuncType, functionResultAfter, getExprType)
import Gopurs.ExprContext (ExprContext, TranslateExpr, bindParameters, flattenStmts)
import Gopurs.GoAst (GoDecl(..), GoExpr(..), GoType(..))
import Gopurs.GoSymbol (GoReference(..), generated)
import Gopurs.GoConversions (boxGoExpr, coerceGoExpr)
import Gopurs.GoFunctions (Parameters, curriedFunction, iterationBindings, loopParameters, namedParameters)
import Gopurs.Int32Loops as Int32Loops
import Gopurs.AffineLoops as AffineLoops
import Gopurs.ArraySnoc as ArraySnoc
import Gopurs.ListFilter as ListFilter
import Gopurs.TailAddLoops as TailAddLoops
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.Codegen.Tco (TcoExpr)

type Worker =
  { ident :: String
  , args :: Array String
  , body :: TcoExpr
  , val :: TcoExpr
  }

-- Use precisely the ABI published by ModuleBindings, including native record
-- projections. A self-recursive singleton gets a loop; peers in larger groups
-- remain ordinary calls. Module bodies begin with no captured local bindings.
declaration :: TranslateExpr -> ExprContext -> Boolean -> Worker -> GoDecl
declaration translate context@{ codegenStateRef, modNameStr, moduleFunctions } isSelfRecursive fn =
  let
    info = Map.lookup fn.ident moduleFunctions
    params = namedParameters fn.args (case info of
      Just signature -> signature.fArgs
      Nothing -> [])
    expectedBodyType = map (functionResultAfter (Array.length fn.args)) (extractExprFuncType (getExprType fn.val))
    loop = if isSelfRecursive then
      [ { ident: fn.ident, loopParams: map fst (loopParameters params), goTypes: map snd params } ]
      else []
    workerContext = context
      { depth = 0
      , bound = bindParameters params Map.empty
      , tcoIdent = Just fn.ident
      , loopCtx = loop
      , options = { isTail: isSelfRecursive, inEffectBlock: false }
      , mbExpectedExprType = expectedBodyType
      , mbExpectedGoType = if Array.null fn.args || resultType == TypeValue then Nothing else Just resultType
      }
    resultType = case info of
      Just signature | Array.length fn.args < Array.length signature.fArgs -> TypeValue
      Just signature -> signature.fRet
      Nothing -> TypeValue
    tailAdd = if isSelfRecursive then
      TailAddLoops.worker translate workerContext fn.ident params resultType fn.body
      else Nothing
    body boxed = case tailAdd of
      Just loopBody -> loopBody
      Nothing ->
        let
          native = case ListFilter.worker context.metadata params resultType fn.val of
            Just filtered -> Just filtered
            Nothing -> ArraySnoc.worker modNameStr fn.ident params resultType fn.body
          result = case native of
            Just lowered -> lowered
            Nothing -> translate workerContext 0 fn.body
          returning = if boxed then boxGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr result.expr result.exprType
            else coerceGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr result.expr result.exprType resultType
          statements = flattenStmts result.stmts <> [ GoReturn returning ]
        in if isSelfRecursive then
          AffineLoops.wrap translate workerContext (AffineLoops.globalTarget modNameStr fn.ident) params resultType fn.body
            (Int32Loops.loop fn.ident params resultType statements)
          else GoBlock (iterationBindings params <> statements)
    value = if Array.null fn.args then
      -- A zero-argument abstraction still defers its whole body until called.
      curriedFunction [ Tuple "_" TypeValue ] TypeValue
        (body true)
      else
        let
          worker = GoFunctionDecl
            { name: generated modNameStr ("Call_" <> modNameStr <> "_" <> fn.ident)
            , params: loopParameters params
            , result: resultType
            , body: body false
            }
        in
          unsafePerformEffect do
            Ref.modify_ (\state -> state { declarations = Array.snoc state.declarations worker }) codegenStateRef
            pure (boxedWrapper context fn.ident params resultType)
  in
    GoCachedValue { identifier: generated modNameStr (modNameStr <> "_" <> fn.ident), expression: value, goType: TypeValue }

-- Module wrappers group up to ten arguments; larger arities keep unary layers.
-- LocalWorkers and anonymous closures retain their own grouping policies.
boxedWrapper :: ExprContext -> String -> Parameters -> GoType -> GoExpr
boxedWrapper { codegenStateRef, modNameStr } name params resultType =
  let
    wrapperParams = map (\(Tuple param _) -> param <> "_box") params
    call = GoCall (GoRef (SymbolReference (generated modNameStr ("Call_" <> modNameStr <> "_" <> name))))
      (map (\(Tuple param ty) -> coerceGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr (GoVar (param <> "_box")) TypeValue ty) params)
    boxed = boxGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr call resultType
    arity = Array.length params
    wrapperName = if arity == 1 then "gopurs_runtime.Func" else "gopurs_runtime.Func" <> show arity
  in
    if arity <= 10 then
      GoCall (GoVar wrapperName) [ GoFuncLit (map (\param -> Tuple param TypeValue) wrapperParams) [] boxed TypeValue ]
    else Array.foldr
      (\param inner -> GoCall (GoSelector (GoVar "gopurs_runtime") "Func")
        [ GoFuncLit [ Tuple param TypeValue ] [] inner TypeValue ])
      boxed wrapperParams

module Main where

-- @dependencies: prelude effect console refs

import Prelude
import Effect (Effect)
import Effect.Console (log, logShow)
import Effect.Ref as Ref

-- Closed record evaluation retains a strict global binding demand even when
-- the caller projects only the integer field.
snapshot :: Int -> { value :: Int, witness :: Unit }
snapshot remaining
  | remaining == 0 = { value: 0, witness: unit }
  | otherwise =
      let previous = snapshot (remaining - 1)
      in { value: previous.value + 1, witness: previous.witness }

effectSnapshot :: Int -> { value :: Int, witness :: String -> Effect Unit }
effectSnapshot remaining
  | remaining == 0 = { value: 0, witness: log }
  | otherwise =
      let previous = effectSnapshot (remaining - 1)
      in { value: previous.value + 1, witness: previous.witness }

rounds :: Int -> Int -> Int
rounds remaining total
  | remaining == 0 = total
  | otherwise = rounds (remaining - 1) (total + (snapshot 7).value)

effectRounds :: Int -> Int -> Int
effectRounds remaining total
  | remaining == 0 = total
  | otherwise = effectRounds (remaining - 1) (total + (effectSnapshot 5).value)

localRounds :: Int -> Int -> Int -> Int
localRounds offset count seed =
  let
    repeat remaining total
      | remaining == 0 = total
      | otherwise = repeat (remaining - 1) (total + (snapshot 11).value)
  in offset + repeat count seed

main :: Effect Unit
main = do
  repetitions <- Ref.new 20
  count <- Ref.read repetitions
  maximum <- Ref.new 2147483647
  maxInt <- Ref.read maximum
  logShow [ rounds 0 maxInt, rounds 1 0, rounds count 0, rounds 5 (-40), rounds 2 maxInt ]
  logShow [ localRounds 3 count 0, localRounds 3 0 (-17), localRounds 0 2 maxInt ]
  logShow [ effectRounds 0 maxInt, effectRounds count 2, effectRounds 2 maxInt ]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read-only verification of the retained State campaign; writes only audit.json."""
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import hashlib
import json
import math
from pathlib import Path
import re
import statistics
import subprocess

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
WORK = HERE.parents[1]
ROOT = WORK.parents[2]
CAMPAIGN = json.loads((WORK / 'campaign/results.json').read_text())


def digest(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def metrics(times, reference):
    ratios = [time / reference[name] for name, time in times.items()]
    return {
        'total': sum(times.values()) / sum(reference.values()),
        'arithmetic': statistics.mean(ratios),
        'median': statistics.median(ratios),
        'geometric': math.exp(statistics.mean(map(math.log, ratios))),
    }


frozen = CAMPAIGN['frozen_reference']
removed_catalogue = 'bin/benchmark/ratio-measurements.json'
source_checks = {}
for name, expected in frozen['source_sha256'].items():
    path = ROOT / name
    if path.exists():
        assert digest(path) == expected, name
        source_checks[name] = 'unchanged'
    else:
        assert name == removed_catalogue, name
        old = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', 'dbd8fc943^:' + name], cwd=ROOT)
        assert hashlib.sha256(old).hexdigest() == expected
        source_checks[name] = 'removed_by_user_commit_dbd8fc943_after_measurement'

compiler = CAMPAIGN['compiler_snapshot']['files_sha256']
for name, expected in compiler.items():
    assert digest(name) == expected, name

binary_checks = {}
for item in CAMPAIGN['core_manifest']['plan']:
    path = Path(item['command'][0])
    assert digest(path) == item['executable_sha256']
    binary_checks['core-' + item['key']] = item['executable_sha256']
for variant, directory in CAMPAIGN['all_campaign']['workspaces'].items():
    expected = CAMPAIGN['all_campaign']['executable_sha256'][variant]
    assert digest(Path(directory) / 'benchmark') == expected
    binary_checks['all-' + variant] = expected
for path, expected in frozen['c_build']['payload_sha256'].items():
    assert digest(path) == expected
    binary_checks['c'] = expected

recalculated = {}
for variant, times in CAMPAIGN['primary_times_us'].items():
    result = metrics(times, frozen['c_times_us'])
    assert len(times) == 14
    assert all(math.isclose(value, CAMPAIGN['aggregates'][variant][name], rel_tol=1e-14)
               for name, value in result.items())
    recalculated[variant] = result

inputs = {}
for variant in ['before', 'after']:
    directory = WORK / 'proofs' / (variant + '-inputs')
    manifest = json.loads((directory / 'manifest.json').read_text())
    assert manifest['binary_sha256'] == binary_checks['core-' + variant]
    assert manifest['c_binary_sha256'] == binary_checks['c']
    assert digest(manifest['generated_source']) == manifest['generated_sha256']
    assert digest(directory / 'opaque-override.go') == manifest['override_sha256']
    assert manifest['cases'] == 88 and manifest['opaque_calls_per_action'] == 1
    cases = json.loads((directory / 'inputs.json').read_text())
    lines = (directory / 'stdout.txt').read_text().splitlines()
    assert len(cases) == len(lines) == 88
    assert not (directory / 'stderr.txt').read_text()
    for case, line in zip(cases, lines):
        name, value, output = line.split()
        assert name == case['name'] and int(value) == case['input']
        int(output)
    inputs[variant] = {'manifest_sha256': digest(directory / 'manifest.json'),
                       'stdout_sha256': digest(directory / 'stdout.txt'),
                       'inputs_sha256': digest(directory / 'inputs.json'),
                       'cases': 88, 'opaque_calls_per_action_reported': 1}
assert inputs['before']['stdout_sha256'] == inputs['after']['stdout_sha256']
assert inputs['before']['inputs_sha256'] == inputs['after']['inputs_sha256']

diagnostic_dir = WORK / 'proofs/regression-isolated-ast-st'
diagnostic = json.loads((diagnostic_dir / 'results.json').read_text())
assert diagnostic['primary_campaign_sha256'] == digest(WORK / 'campaign/results.json')
diagnostic_checks = {}
for key, case in diagnostic['cases'].items():
    assert len(case['runs']) == 6
    assert case['order'] == ['before', 'after', 'after', 'before', 'before', 'after']
    for index, run in enumerate(case['runs'], 1):
        prefix = diagnostic_dir / (key + '-' + str(index) + '-' + run['variant'])
        stdout = Path(str(prefix) + '.stdout').read_text()
        stderr = Path(str(prefix) + '.stderr').read_text()
        assert stdout == run['stdout'] and stderr == run['stderr'] == ''
        output = re.search(r'\(Output & Warm-up\)\s+(-?\d+)\s+\(Execution time', stdout)
        assert output and int(output[1]) == case['expected']
    diagnostic_checks[key] = {'oracles': 6, 'expected': case['expected'],
                             'medians_us': case['medians_us'],
                             'change_percent': case['change_percent']}

report = {
    'checked_at_utc': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
    'mode': 'read-only verification; no build, test execution or new timing',
    'campaign_sha256': digest(WORK / 'campaign/results.json'),
    'script_sha256': digest(__file__),
    'frozen_sources': {'count': len(source_checks),
                       'unchanged': sum(value == 'unchanged' for value in source_checks.values()),
                       'intentional_post_campaign_removals': [removed_catalogue],
                       'checks': source_checks},
    'compiler_snapshot': {'checked': len(compiler), 'all_unchanged': True},
    'binary_sha256': binary_checks,
    'recalculated_go_c': recalculated,
    'runtime_input_proofs': inputs,
    'runtime_input_note': 'The retained 88 before/after outputs agree. C comparisons and opacity-call counts were reported by the original proof; this audit checks its preserved artifacts and exact C/generated-source/overlay hashes without re-execution.',
    'isolated_diagnostics': diagnostic_checks,
    'persistent_evidence': ['campaign/core', 'campaign/all', 'proofs/before-inputs',
                            'proofs/after-inputs', 'proofs/production-generated',
                            'proofs/regression-generated-compare',
                            'proofs/regression-isolated-ast-st', 'compiler-before'],
    'temporary_evidence_limit': 'Original /tmp collection-wrapper and compiler-validation logs are no longer present. Preserved campaign outputs and proof files remain intact; new validation reruns are tracked separately by the parent task.',
}
(HERE / 'audit.json').write_text(json.dumps(report, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + '\n')
print(json.dumps({key: report[key] for key in ['compiler_snapshot', 'recalculated_go_c', 'isolated_diagnostics']}, indent=2))
print('523 frozen entries checked: 522 unchanged, one intentional catalogue removal. Both 88-input proofs and 12 isolated oracles verified.')
